metadata.name: dsh-auto-vision

paragraphs.text: Let a text-only model see images by automatically calling a vision model from the same provider.
# dsh-auto-vision
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-auto-sight) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-auto-sight)
**English** | 简体中文
Let a text-only model see images. When the selected model has no image input, or recognition is unus
able (for example the call fails or returns nothing), **Auto Vision** asks another image-capable mod
el on the same provider to read each image, then sends the original request with that description in
place of the image.
A DSH plugin. No API keys are stored in or sent by the plugin itself — it uses the credential your p
rovider config already points at.
## Why this instead of another vision setup
- **No second API to configure.** It reuses the provider you are already talking to — no extra key,

base URL or proxy to set up.
- **No model IDs to look up.** It reads that provider's model list and

finds an image-capable one by itself; naming one in Settings is optional.
- **Fixes the rejected dro
p.** Dragging an image into a text-only model's input box used to be refused. Now the image is read
first, and the same model answers.
## What it does
- Hooks `llm/stream`: if a request carries image blocks and the selected route is text-only, each im
age is read by a vision model on the **same provider** and replaced with a text block `[Image #n int

erpreted by <model>] … [/Image #n]`.
- Only steps in when all three are true: the request has at lea
st one `image` block, the main route does not declare `image`, and a vision target resolves on the s

ame provider. Otherwise it passes through untouched.
- If the main model can already see images, it
passes through by default. Select a vision model and enable *Use the vision model even when the main
model can see images* to have that model read first anyway. The switch has no effect when no vision

model is selected.
- Target order: the model chosen in Settings → other mounted image-capable model
s on the same provider → name-matched candidates from the official `/models` list. The next group is

tried only when the previous one is unavailable or has failed.
- If the chosen vision model fails,
tries the remaining targets in order; the block is marked `after <failed model> failed`. A system no

tice asks the main model to tell the user which model failed and which one was used.
- If every moun
ted vision model fails, queries the provider's official `/models` list, keeps name-matched candidate
s, and tries them over the direct endpoint. The official list has no modality metadata, so these can

didates are not guaranteed to accept images.
- Sends a model that is not mounted locally, or is know
n to the adapter as text-only, to the provider's OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint. Thi

s requires `baseURL` and a usable `apiKeyEnv` in the provider config.
- If every vision model fails,
inserts `[Image #n could not be interpreted by any vision model: …]` and still asks the main model
to report it; the turn continues, and one failed image does not stop the others in the same message.
- Advertises image input in the model picker for text routes that have a vision sibling, so you can

attach an image to them directly.
- Session history and the UI keep the real image; only the reques

t going to the text model is rewritten.
[该节后续省略]
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or install it from the plugin marketplace.
The same code is published to npm as `dsh-auto-sight` (`npm i dsh-auto-sight`). The npm build is pre
built — no install-time build step or `allowBuilds` prompt — and its download count is visible on th
all-time build step or `allowBuilds` prompt — and its download count is visible on the package page.
## Settings
**Settings → Auto Vision**: pick the vision model (grouped per provider), or leave it on *Automatic*
. The selection is stored in volatile config and applies to the next image request. After selecting
a vision model, you can enable *Use the vision model even when the main model can see images*; it ha
s no effect while no model is selected.
| Config key | Default | Meaning |
| `visionProvider` / `visionModel` | empty = auto | Model to read images with. A selection made for
another provider is ignored; the plugin discovers a target on the provider handling the request inst

ead. |
| `preferVisionModel` | `false` | Use the selected vision model even when the main model can

see images; only applies when a vision model is selected. |
| `timeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-image read

only applies when a vision model is selected. |
| `timeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-image read timeout. |
The picker has three groups:

- **Guaranteed**: models whose DSH config declares `input: [text, image]`.
- **Configured without im
age input**: models present in the DSH config but not declared as image-capable; shown by name match

.
- **Official candidates**: the `/models` endpoint exposes no modality metadata, so these are name-
matched guesses and are collapsed by default.
[该节后续省略]
## Privacy
- Images are sent only to the vision model of the **same provider** you are already talking to. Noth

ing goes to a third-party service.
- Credentials are read at request time from the credential refere
nce (`apiKeyEnv`) of that provider's config; the key never enters the plugin's config, logs, or the

browser UI.
- Image descriptions are cached in memory for the session only, and are never written to

r UI.
- Image descriptions are cached in memory for the session only, and are never written to disk.
## Limitations

- Same provider only: a vision model on a different API is not used.
- The official list exposes onl
y basic fields such as model IDs, not modality metadata; *candidates* are name-matched and may fail.

Direct calls also need `baseURL` and a usable `apiKeyEnv` in the provider config.
- One extra model

call per uncached image.
- Auto-marking modifies the `llm-pi-ai` model config; if several Settings
pages edit config concurrently, a revision conflict is possible. That attempt only logs a warning an

d does not retry, and it does not affect the answer.
- Image content is treated as untrusted data in
the vision prompt (the model is told not to follow instructions found in the image), but the result
ing text still flows into your model's context as evidence.
